title.full: What happens when CPF payouts start

summary.text: For people born in 1958 or later, CPF savings may move to the Retirement Account and support CPF LIFE payouts.

details.heading: Ordinary Account savings
details.body: If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum, your Ordinary Account savings will move to your Retirement Account to make up the sum in cash. This helps you receive higher payouts.

details.heading: CPF LIFE premium
details.body: When you join CPF LIFE, your Retirement Account savings pay your CPF LIFE premium. The premium continues to earn interest, which is included in your lifetime monthly payouts.

details.heading: Amount available at 65
details.body: Up to 20% of your Retirement Account savings at 65 can be withdrawn immediately. If you do not withdraw it or use it to increase your payouts, it will move to your Ordinary Account for future cash withdrawals.

sources.page_title: What will happen to my CPF savings when my monthly payouts start?

quotes.text: If you are born on or after 1958, the following will happen when your monthly payouts start:

If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), your Ordinary Account savings will be transferred to your Retirement Account to make up your FRS in cash. This will help you receive higher payouts.

When you join CPF LIFE, your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used to pay your CPF LIFE premium. Your premium will continue to earn interest and the interest earned will be factored into your lifetime monthly payouts.

Up to 20% of your RA savings at 65 will be available for your immediate withdrawable from age 65. If this withdrawable amount is not withdrawn nor used to increase your payouts, it will be transferred to your Ordinary Account for future cash withdrawals.
